    fix(android): list only folders the emulator can actually boot
    
    The library listed any folder that had a PS3 title's SHAPE -- a PARAM.SFO
    somewhere, USRDIR beside it, CATEGORY other than GD -- which is not the same
    thing as a game. A shared folder is full of folders that pass that test and
    cannot be played: PS3 homebrew is several titles apiece, so Cheat Engine alone
    lands as CEFramework / CEHtmlApi / CEHtmlUI / CEPhWeb, next to log directories
    and PS1 ROM sets and every other app's leftovers.
    
    Every one of those is also a tile that can only fail. _rpcsx_boot resolves a
    directory through locateEbootPath and, finding nothing, hands the bare
    directory to Emu.BootGame, which answers invalid_file_or_folder. So the junk
    in the list and "Game failed to start: InvalidFileOrFolder" on tap are the
    same bug, and the fix is the same fix.
    
    The bar applied here is the one the core already applies in fetchGameInfo
    (rpcsx-android.cpp): BOOTABLE set, a TITLE_ID, and an EBOOT the core can open.
    hasBootableEboot mirrors locateEbootPath's four candidates, so the scanner and
    the core cannot disagree about a folder. Listing less than the core can boot is
    the failure that costs the most time: an unbootable tile reads as a broken
    emulator rather than a folder that was never a game.

    fix(android): list only folders the emulator can actually boot
    
    The library listed any folder that had a PS3 title's SHAPE -- a PARAM.SFO
    somewhere, USRDIR beside it, CATEGORY other than GD -- which is not the same
    thing as a game. A shared folder is full of folders that pass that test and
    cannot be played: PS3 homebrew is several titles apiece, so Cheat Engine alone
    lands as CEFramework / CEHtmlApi / CEHtmlUI / CEPhWeb, next to log directories
    and PS1 ROM sets and every other app's leftovers.
    
    Every one of those is also a tile that can only fail. _rpcsx_boot resolves a
    directory through locateEbootPath and, finding nothing, hands the bare
    directory to Emu.BootGame, which answers invalid_file_or_folder. So the junk
    in the list and "Game failed to start: InvalidFileOrFolder" on tap are the
    same bug, and the fix is the same fix.
    
    The bar applied here is the one the core already applies in fetchGameInfo
    (rpcsx-android.cpp): BOOTABLE set, a TITLE_ID, and an EBOOT the core can open.
    hasBootableEboot mirrors locateEbootPath's four candidates, so the scanner and
    the core cannot disagree about a folder. Listing less than the core can boot is
    the failure that costs the most time: an unbootable tile reads as a broken
    emulator rather than a folder that was never a game.
    
    Two things deliberately do NOT become stricter:
    
      - An unreadable PARAM.SFO proves nothing, so a parse failure falls back to the
        old structural answer. A truncated SFO must not hide a real game.
      - No USRDIR requirement. locateEbootPath also accepts an EBOOT.BIN beside the
        SFO, so requiring USRDIR was a second, stricter rule that hid games the
        emulator boots perfectly well.
    
    The SAF path gets the structural half for the same reason; CATEGORY and BOOTABLE
    are not read there, because a document tree has no path to open the SFO with.
    
    ScanSchemaVersion 8 -> 9: the cache holds the scan RESULT, so without the bump
    every existing install keeps serving the junk and never rescans.
    
    Also, on the launch side:
      - _rpcsx_boot logs a directory it could not resolve to an EBOOT, naming the
        folder and the four paths it tried. That case was completely silent, and it
        is the whole explanation for the error the user sees.
      - The failure toast now distinguishes the three causes behind
        InvalidFileOrFolder: a folder with no EBOOT, a file that cannot be read
        (grant All files access), and a file that is not a disc.
    
    Verified against 22 fixtures driving the shipped isPs3GameFolder/ParamSfo
    (extracted verbatim into a JVM harness): real installed games, JB rips, PSN
    games and an EBOOT at the folder root all stay listed; no-EBOOT, BOOTABLE=0,
    no-TITLE_ID, CATEGORY=GD and SFO-without-payload are all filtered; truncated
    and zero-byte SFOs still fall back to being listed.

    directory to Emu.BootGame, which answers invalid_file_or_folder. So the junk
    in the list and "Game failed to start: InvalidFileOrFolder" on tap are the
    same bug, and the fix is the same fix.

    the core cannot disagree about a folder. Listing less than the core can boot is

import java.io.File
import java.nio.ByteBuffer
import java.nio.ByteOrder
import java.nio.file.Files

/**
 * A PARAM.SFO writer, so the fixtures below are real files parsed by the real
 * parser rather than a mocked answer.
 */
fun sfo(vararg entries: Pair<String, ByteArray>): ByteArray {
    val keys = entries.map { it.first }
    val keyTableSize = 20 + entries.size * 16
    val keyTable = 20
    val dataTable = keyTable + keyTableSize - 20
    val dataBlob = entries.map { it.second }
    val dataOffsets = mutableListOf(0)
    for (i in 0 until dataBlob.size - 1) dataOffsets += dataOffsets[i] + dataBlob[i].size
    val total = dataTable + dataOffsets.last() + dataBlob.last().size

    val buf = ByteBuffer.allocate(total).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
    buf.putInt(0x46535000)          // "\0PSF"
    buf.putInt(4, 20)               // key table start
    buf.putInt(8, keyTable)         // key table start
    buf.putInt(12, dataTable)       // data table start
    buf.putInt(16, entries.size)   // entry count

    var keyCursor = keyTable + 20
    entries.forEachIndexed { i, (key, value) ->
        val e = keyTable + i * 16
        buf.putShort(e, (keyCursor - keyTable).toShort())          // key offset
        buf.putShort(e + 2, 0)                                     // align
        buf.putShort(e + 4, 0)                                     // format
        buf.putInt(e + 8, value.size)                              // length
        buf.putInt(e + 12, dataOffsets[i])                         // data offset
        buf.put(key.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
        buf.put(0)
        keyCursor += key.size + 1
    }
    dataBlob.forEachIndexed { i, bytes -> buf.put(dataTable + dataOffsets[i], bytes) }
    return buf.array()
}

private fun le32(v: Int) = ByteBuffer.allocate(4).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).putInt(v).array()

private fun sfoEntry(vararg entries: Pair<String, ByteArray>): ByteArray = sfo(*entries)

fun gameSfo(titleId: String, category: String = "HG", bootable: Int = 1) = sfoEntry(
    "BOOTABLE" to le32(bootable),

    "TITLE_ID" to titleId.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8),
    "TITLE" to "Some Game".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8),
)

/** Materialise a tree given as a path -> contents map ("a/b/c" -> bytes | null for a dir). */
fun tree(spec: Map<String, ByteArray?>): File {
    val root = Files.createTempDirectory("xeno-fixture").toFile()
    for ((path, content) in spec) {
        val file = File(root, path)
        file.parentFile.mkdirs()
        if (content == null) {
            file.mkdirs()
        } else {
            file.writeBytes(content)
        }
    }
    return root
}

private var failures = 0
private var checks = 0

private fun expect(label: String, want: Any?, got: Any?) {
    checks++
    if (want != got) {
        failures++
        println("FAIL  $label: want $want, got $got")
    } else {
        println("ok    $label = $got")
    }
}

package harness

import java.io.File
import java.nio.ByteBuffer
import java.nio.ByteOrder
import java.nio.file.Files

/**
 * A PARAM.SFO writer matching rpcs3/Loader/PSF.cpp exactly:
 *
 *   header_t  (20 bytes): magic, version 0x101, off_key_table, off_data_table, entries_num
 *   def_table_t (16 bytes): u16 key_off, u16 param_fmt, u32 param_len, u32 param_max, u32 data_off
 *
 * key_off and data_off are relative to off_key_table and off_data_table respectively, and
 * the key table runs from off_key_table to off_data_table with every key NUL-terminated.
 */
private const val FMT_STRING = 0x0204
private const val FMT_INTEGER = 0x0404

class Entry(val key: String, val fmt: Int, val maxSize: Int, val value: ByteArray)

fun str(key: String, text: String) = Entry(key, FMT_STRING, text.length + 1, text.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
fun num(key: String, v: Int) = Entry(key, FMT_INTEGER, 4, ByteBuffer.allocate(4).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).putInt(v).array())

fun sfo(entries: List<Entry>): ByteArray {
    val indexStart = 20
    val keyTable = indexStart
    val keyBytes = entries.joinToString("") { it.key + "\u0000" }.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)
    val dataTable = keyTable + keyBytes.size

    val dataOffsets = mutableListOf(0)
    val padded = entries.map { it.value.copyOf(it.maxSize) }
    for (i in 0 until padded.size - 1) dataOffsets += dataOffsets[i] + padded[i].size
    val total = dataTable + dataOffsets.last() + padded.last().size

    val buf = ByteBuffer.allocate(total).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
    buf.putInt(0, 0x46535000)          // "\0PSF"
    buf.putInt(4, 0x101)
    buf.putInt(8, keyTable)
    buf.putInt(12, dataTable)
    buf.putInt(16, entries.size)

    var keyCursor = 0
    entries.forEachIndexed { i, e ->
        val off = indexStart + i * 16
        buf.putShort(off, keyCursor.toShort())                 // key_off, relative to key table
        buf.putShort(off + 2, e.fmt.toShort())                 // param_fmt
        buf.putInt(off + 4, e.value.size)                     // param_len
        buf.putInt(off + 8, e.maxSize)                        // param_max
        buf.putInt(off + 12, dataOffsets[i])                  // data_off, relative to data table
        keyCursor += e.key.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).size + 1
    }
    buf.put(keyTable, keyBytes)
    padded.forEachIndexed { i, bytes -> buf.put(dataTable + dataOffsets[i], bytes) }
    return buf.array()
}

fun gameSfo(titleId: String, category: String = "HG", bootable: Int = 1) = sfo(
    listOf(
        num("BOOTABLE", bootable),
        str("CATEGORY", category),
        str("TITLE_ID", titleId),
        str("TITLE", "Some Game"),
    )
)
